chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who buys goods for a deferred period, he said: 'It is not permissible for him to sell it with markup (murabahah) except for the same period for which he bought it. And if he sells it with markup and does not inform the buyer, the buyer is entitled to the same option (of keeping it at the original price or returning it).'

key_terms.إِلَى الْأَجَلِ الَّذِي اشْتَرَاهُ إِلَي: to the period for which he bought it
key_terms.مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ: the same (referring to the option of returning or keeping)
key_terms.يَشْتَرِي الْمَتَاعَ إِلَى أَجَلٍ: buys goods for a deferred period

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for selling goods bought on credit with a profit margin in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *Murabaha* (selling at a markup) for goods originally acquired on credit, provided the new buyer also pays in deferred installments for an equivalent duration. It establishes that if the seller conceals the markup, the buyer retains the right of option (*Khiyar*) to rescind the contract, ensuring transparency in credit-based transactions. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between simple credit sales and interest-based speculation, emphasizing fairness in deferred payment agreements.
